Pinar Sayin is a Turkish ceramic artist based in Prague and the founder of Pinpottery. Her work brings architectural geometry into functional ceramics, transforming teapots, cups, and vessels into sculptural objects defined by clean edges, bold angles, carved surfaces, and carefully chosen glazes. Using techniques such as handbuilding, mold-making, and slip-casting, she maintains remarkable precision while ensuring that every piece remains practical and comfortable to use. The result sits beautifully between pottery, sculpture, and functional design. Artist: @Pinpottery  #art #ceramics #pottery #artist #design

Here are a few helpful tips:  • poke a small hole so that as it dries and shrinks, air can release safely. • push in your flange on a straight edge, not a curve. • you don’t have to have a knob on top. pricing my work is truly my LEAST favourite thing 😭  especially after trying to look closer at the numbers behind my small ceramic business. i’m trying to map out the potential 1, 3, and 5 year revenue and expense projections to see if investing in a kiln and building this business actually makes any sense. at my current $30-$65 price point, i’m losing money selling my work and cannot justify a kiln. i’ve made the terrifying decision to raise my prices by 25-30%. the money will go towards expanding production (investing. in a kiln & shelving), upgrading my website, expanding to ship to the US, and finally, offering private lessons and workshops.  with the price increase, I will still need to survive 6 months - 1 year without a livable wage / making profit. i’ll be focusing on my higher-margin petal bowls and bring in some more affordable $25 products like spoon rests and trinket dishes to keep things as accessible as possible. my mugs are not viable as they take me 2hrs each, but i’m going to keep making them for now and hope i can speed it up. no more lidded jars outside of speciality collections as the margins are too low.  i’m also going to try to secure 1-2 freelance social media clients to provide me with some supplement income as a buffer. this is the behind the scenes of small ceramics business’ that you normally don’t see, because it’s not nearly as cute or fun as the pots themselves. #potterybusiness #ceramics #smallbusiness #priceincrease #handmadeceramics
